- When sentiment is consistently low or neutral (≤0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap upward momentum at 3–5% above peak or reduce slope.
- If sentiment turns bullish (≥0.8) mid-period, model frequently overestimates future highs; apply downward bias to later forecast days, especially if sentiment stabilizes.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–4 days; if sentiment shows clear reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2), adjust forecast to align with 1–2 prior-day closing price.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early days (1–7) when sentiment is rising; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for first 5 days if sentiment >0.7.
- If sentiment is flat or declining (≤0.3) for 3+ days, model overpredicts short-term volatility; smooth forecast curve and reduce volatility amplitude by 20–40%.
